source_judgments: EXTERNAL retains four entity roles, including noncallable block data, the two-by-two procedure/use matrix and all four declaration mechanisms.
An interface body supplying EXTERNAL in its containing context is distinct from an inner own-procedure respecification prohibited by C844.
C846 retains all fifteen variable-definition contexts; C847 retains all four pointer-association context families. Their canonical inventories remain pending.

C848 retains nonintrinsic procedure and allocatable-coarray/subobject conditions; C849 retains all three intrinsic synchronization types, surrounding coarray requirements and competing-cause isolation.
IN restrictions cover invocation and execution. Pointer association is distinct from target-value mutability, and other-route deallocation does not license an undefined-association inquiry.
OUT entry states, actual definability/form and whole-invoking-statement interference are separate requirements. INOUT does not inherit OUT entry changes, and omitted INTENT is not INOUT.
Nonpointer subobjects inherit INTENT; a pointer component as a pointer is a subobject, but its target is not.
S8.5.10-003 and -005 remain undefined-result/context-only. Existing default-initialization and finalization effects retain their original owners, valid observations and roles.
All notes remain informative, including note4.2. Optional checking and optimization do not become compulsory diagnoses, traps or generated-code promises.

The review's19.6.2 qualification is explicit in the view and source adjudication: zero-sized arrays and zero-length strings are always defined. This supplies no presence, allocation, association or undefinedness oracle.
